#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`; for a noted block, no `--note`), a correction that
names no block or more than one, two blocks for one entry in one call.
Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the record file and its
history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'

# Rung S record: a comparison at a NaN or at 0/0 answers false

## Findings

1. **The overview of operators now says what both paths answer at a NaN and at 0/0.** Claim: `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:284-291` says that `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` return `false` if either rational argument is 0/0 (the infinities ordered, -1/0 below and 1/0 above every finite rational value), and `false` if either floating-point argument is a NaN, with `CMP` `Unordered`; the callout `:292-300` and the Appendix I entry "A comparison at a NaN or at the rational indefinite" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4550-4622`, `\seclabel{revival-nan-comparison}`) keep the Working Draft's raise (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:274-278`). Conditions: walk at `RR64`, `RR32` and `QQ`; compiled at the helpers `doubleLT` to `doubleGE` and `floatLT` to `floatGE` (the compiler's own library has no `QQ` and no `CMP` on floats until the switch-over, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:35`, `:231`). Evidence: `ProjectFortress/tests/ComparisonAtNaNWalk.fss` ('OK (time = 773ms)', `harness-one.sh` at 4d27fbcc5's code); `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled.fss:101-112` and `NativeHelperFamilyRR32Compiled.fss:256-267` ('OK (4 tests)', `ONE_JVM=1 .../junit.sh nan ProjectFortress/compiler_tests NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled.test NativeHelperFamilyRR32Compiled.test`). Means: row 672 closes (P-159); no program changes; `FloatingComparisonError` and `RationalComparisonError` stay declared and unused (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1184`, `:1187`).
2. **Under walk, 0/0 compared with itself answers `true` for `<=` and `>=` too, beside row 440's `=` and `CMP`.** Conditions: `QQ` under walk. Evidence: `QQ`'s `opr <=(self, other:QQ) = (self < other) OR (self = other)` and `opr >=` from it (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:605`, `:607`), with `=` true at 0/0 (`:597-598`); the planner's `NanQQ.fss` at a3252d568: '0/0 <= 0/0 true 0/0 >= 0/0 true 0/0 < 0/0 false 0/0 = 0/0 true 0/0 CMP 0/0 EqualTo' (CLIMB-BATCH-26.md, "The planner's probes"). Means: the new overview sentence ("returns false if either argument is 0/0") departs from walk at this one case; the Appendix I entry's Effect and the callout name it, with row 440.
3. **The team's later restart carries the original sentences.** `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/Operators/operator-overview.tick:274-278` says a rational comparison throws `RationalComparisonError` at 1/0 or 0/0 and a float one `FloatingComparisonError` at a NaN, word for word the Working Draft's. Means: it now disagrees with `Specification/`; this rung's files leave it (a question for the curator).

## For FACTS

**A comparison at a NaN or at 0/0 answers `false`, on the specification's word too.** The overview of operators says that `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` return `false` at a floating-point NaN and at the rational 0/0, that `CMP` returns `Unordered` at a NaN, and that -1/0 and 1/0 are ordered below and above every finite rational (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:284-291`; Appendix I, "A comparison at a NaN or at the rational indefinite"); both paths answer so and nothing raises `FloatingComparisonError` or `RationalComparisonError` (P-159). Walk departs at 0/0 against itself, `true` for `=`, `<=`, `>=` (row 440). Test: `ProjectFortress/tests/ComparisonAtNaNWalk.fss`, and the NaN asserts of `compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled.fss` and `NativeHelperFamilyRR32Compiled.fss`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-nan-comparison/REPORT.md`, sections 1 and 2.

## The ledger

- Row 672: close, by the commit `1d109308e` (or its merged successor), test `ProjectFortress/tests/ComparisonAtNaNWalk.fss`, `--settled "P-159: the overview's float and rational sentences revised in Appendix I's form to false and Unordered"`.
- Row 440: its whole new line, for `ledger.py rewrite 440` (the note asked for does not fit: the notes cell is 676 of 700 characters; the line below passes `ledger.py check --rows`, '1 rows, 0 fail the template'):

| 440 | under `walk`, `QQ` answers 0/0 compared with itself with `true` for `=`, `<=` and `>=`, and with `EqualTo` for `CMP`, where the specification makes 0/0 unordered with itself, so that the five comparisons are false and `CMP` answers `Unordered` | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library gap vs spec (library) | `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex`, "Rational Numbers"; `basic/operators/opr-overview.tex`, "Comparisons Operators" | `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXRationalUnorderedRungP.fss` | climb batch 6 rung T and its skeptic | `QQ`'s `opr =` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:597-598` at 4d27fbcc5) compares numerators and denominators, under the team's comment "0/0 = 0/0 is supposed to be true (//unlike// the behavior of floating-point NaN)" (`:596`); its `<=` and `>=` (`:605`, `:607`) and `StandardPartialOrder`'s `CMP` (`:224-229`) answer from it, while `0/0 < 0/0` is `false` and `0/0 CMP 1` `Unordered`. `MIN`, `MAX` and `MINMAX` (`:610-619`), `MINNUM` and `MAXNUM` (`:658-661`) find 0/0 by `=`. The prelude has no `QQ`. `<=`, `>=`: '0/0 <= 0/0 true 0/0 >= 0/0 true' (`NanQQ.fss` at a3252d568). Full text: history, row 440 |

- New rows: none.

## Handover

Rung S (climb batch 26): the operators overview's two comparison sentences revised to the rationals chapter's reading, a NaN or 0/0 comparing `false` and the rational infinities ordered (P-159), with Appendix I's entry "A comparison at a NaN or at the rational indefinite" and the decision record; row 672 closes on `ComparisonAtNaNWalk`; row 440 rewritten to name `<=` and `>=`; the later restart's copy (`Documentation/.../operator-overview.tick:274-278`) still says the raise.

## Revival change

**The change.** The team's specification, `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:274-278`, says that a comparison of rational values throws `RationalComparisonError` if either argument is 1/0 or 0/0, and that a comparison of floating-point values throws `FloatingComparisonError` if either argument is a NaN; its rationals chapter says instead that 0/0 compares `false` "for compatibility with floating-point arithmetic" and that the infinities are ordered (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:372-378`), and the team's walk and compiler answer `false` and never raise (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1187`, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:99` declare the error; nothing throws it). The tree's specification now says that `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` return `false` at a NaN or at 0/0, that `CMP` returns `Unordered` at a NaN, and that -1/0 lies below and 1/0 above every finite rational (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:284-291`); walk and the compiled helpers do so, shown by `ProjectFortress/tests/ComparisonAtNaNWalk.fss` and the NaN asserts of `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled.fss` and `NativeHelperFamilyRR32Compiled.fss`. Walk still answers `true` for 0/0 `=`, `<=` and `>=` 0/0 (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:597-607`). The reason: both implementations and the rationals chapter already gave `false`; Java, Swift, Python, Julia and Haskell answer `false`; a NaN test in software costs 15 to 20 percent of a comparison on unboxed doubles in Java (`explorations/perf-probes/nan-check-cost/REPORT.md:95`).

- F-277 **The compiled checker's overloading exclusion test reads the `self` of a trait whose self type comes from its F-bound as `C[\X\] & X`, and each static parameter at the top of the two domains' meet as its declared bounds; every other rule of overloading keeps the plain signatures.** It builds P-157. The second arrow is made from the declaration's own parameters (`FunctionalMethod.ast`) only where they differ from `parameters()` (`scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala`), and the bounds are read in one more conjunct of the reduction's constraint, alone and never beside the parameter (`scala_src/types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala`, `meetEmptyWithBounds`, a third way to be valid in `OverloadingOracle.excludes`). With the full check on, the 8 pairs between `AdditiveGroup`'s `+` and `-` and the generic scalar block clear (191 to 183, no library line), and the count stage under it is 98. `tint` stays refused, `Box[\Bottom\]` being an instance of both domains (row 786); row 713's pair is accepted and runs, and walk refuses it at load; walk refuses at load the vector pairs' shape in a program's own component (row 804). Gated by `compiler_tests/Exclusion*`, `XXXExclusion*` and `OverloadTwoBoundsClosedTraitExclusion`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-self-type-exclusion/REPORT.md` sections 1, 2 and 4.
- F-252 **Under walk, where the parameter-by-parameter check refuses two declarations with static parameters of their own, the load check reads the pair again on its declared domains, by the No Duplicates, Return Type and Meet Rules.** A declaration with static parameters of its own is a generic function, a generic object's constructor, or a functional method that declares static parameters in a trait or object that has none. Walk's load check first compares two overloads parameter by parameter, and a pair that it finds excluding loads. It reads two generic functions of one name and one list of static parameters at one shared symbolic instantiation, and two instances of one generic object as two object types that cannot be extended, so they exclude. So `o[\T\](x: P[\T\])` beside `o[\T\](x: Q[\T\])`, with `trait P[\T\] excludes { Q[\T\] }`, excludes at one `T`, though a type that extends `P[\ZZ32\]` and `Q[\String\]` has both. Walk then reads such an exclusion again over the instances of each, and withdraws it where their instances do not exclude. Instances of one generic type exclude only where their static arguments cannot be equal. Any other exclusion stands where the two still exclude with their static parameters renamed apart. Or, read at the shared instantiation, it stands where every generic type that both extend forces their static arguments to be equal, since no type extends two instances of one generic trait: so `Array` and `ImmutableArray` exclude at every pair of instances through `ReadableArray`. A pair whose exclusion is withdrawn is read on its declared domains as a refused pair is. It reads a refused pair of two such declarations again, each over all its own instances, and loads the pair if it meets the three rules. A pair that the parameter check orders is read again only for the No Duplicates Rule (F-274). F-275 holds the Return Type Rule. The parameter check does not find two instances of one generic type at different ground static arguments excluding, such as `Tg[\3\]` and `Tg[\4\]`, so two plain declarations so typed are refused (row 416). Two declarations with static parameters of their own so typed load where the reading of the whole parameter type finds the instances apart, as `h[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\])` beside `h[\J\](a: Array[\ZZ32,J\])` loads and runs (F-155, F-258). For the Meet Rule, walk looks for a third declaration that covers the overlap only where, at each position, the two parameter types are equal, or one of them is a static parameter, or both are instances of one generic type whose static arguments match in the same way (row 539). This search reads a bound that names its own parameter from the declarations, so two such bounds meet, and unifies a symbolic size with a size parameter (`types/SymbolicNat.unifyStaticArg`). A pair whose domains exclude when read whole also loads, where neither declaration has a `where` clause of its own (F-258; row 787). A pair with a varargs parameter is not read again and keeps the parameter check's refusal (F-257). At a call, walk compares a functional method of a generic trait or object on the instance that the call makes. It compares a generic dotted method in the same way, except where exactly one of the two declared domains lies inside the other; there it chooses the inner one (F-253). Gated by `tests/DispatchRenamedGenericArmWalk`, `DispatchSwappedGenericArmWalk` and `GenericPairNestedBoundsWalk` (load and dispatch), and the expected failure `XXXOverloadExistentialMeetWalk` (row 539); for the withdrawal, as refusals at load, by `GenericBoundsNoMeetWalk`, `NoDuplicatesRuleWalk`, `NoDuplicatesRuleSizeWalk` and `GenericOverloadInstancesApartWalk`, and as programs that load, by `GenericBoundsMeetWalk`, `GenericFBoundsMeetWalk`, `GenericPairExcludingWalk`, `GenericSizePairNestedWalk`, `ShuffleTest` and `GenericPairExcludesTogetherWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-generic-pairs/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 5; `compile-ladder/rung-walk-overload-if/REPORT.md` section 1, "Row 373", and section 9.

Measured once, on climb batch 25's base (`97a416b18`) with the code generator as landed, by `compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/codegen.sh` with the base's 173 helper strings put back on their glue classes; the base's code generator gave 50 in 14 kinds in the same session. The three kinds that F-315 removes, `Any` in an `extends` clause, `forbid` and the `test` modifier, no longer occur. A declaration counted at its first wall, and no emitted class was run. Each kind left has a ledger row or a plan line, among them a local function (row 304), varargs (row 624), `asif` (row 818) and "Not in the trait table" (row 733), so after the switch-over the code generator still stands between the library and bytecode. On climb batch 21b's base (`aa5c67d48`) the dispatch generator refused none of `FortressLibrary`'s 178 overload sets. No test checks it, since the gate's distance stage runs no code generation. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-codegen-walls/REPORT.md`, "5. Programs run old against new, and the probes"; `reviews/phase3-exit/zero-audit.md`, "Part C. The debt carried into phase 4", item 4; `perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md`, sections 2 to 6.
- F-181 **The code generator compiles a function, method, object or trait declaration that carries a `where` clause in its own header, emitting nothing for the clause, and refuses every function or method with a contract (row 701).** The clause's constraints are the checker's. A trait's or object's contract does not reach the refusal: the disambiguator drops it (row 781); F-255 says how each path reads a `where` clause on an `extends` entry (row 774). #!/bin/bash
# harness-one.sh <scratch-dir> <file.fss>... : rung C's harness-one.sh (explorations/compile-ladder/
# rung-interp-coercion/, itself rung I's shape): the testSystem harness (SystemJUTest, the class build.xml's
# testSystem shards run) over a directory holding only the named test files, with the JVM settings of
# build.xml's systemShard macro and a private cache. Run from FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh.
#
# The scratch directory is deleted when the call starts and when it ends. The private cache is the folder
# <scratch-dir>.cache beside it, kept between calls. A call starts from what that folder holds when it was
# filled under the implementation now built (ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp, which ant compileAll
# writes) and from the Fortress sources now on the source path outside the scratch directory (the .fss and
# .fsi files of Library, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin, ProjectFortress/test_library and ProjectFortress);
# otherwise it empties the folder first. COLD_CACHE=1 empties it in any case. The folder is stamped only when
# the JVM ends normally, so a call that is killed leaves it to be emptied by the next one.
set -u
S=$(realpath -m -- "${1:?scratch dir}") ; shift
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:?}
C=$S.cache
BUILT=$FH/ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp
sources_key () {
    ( cd "$FH" && { find Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin ProjectFortress/test_library -type f -name '*.fs[si]' -print0
                    find ProjectFortress -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.fs[si]' -print0 ; } \
        | sort -z | xargs -0 -r sha1sum | sha1sum | cut -c1-40 )
}
key () { [ -f "$BUILT" ] && echo "$(head -1 "$BUILT") sources $(sources_key)" ; }
rm -rf "$S" ; mkdir -p "$S/tests" "$S/tmp"
KEY=$(key)
if [ -z "${COLD_CACHE:-}" ] && [ -n "$KEY" ] && [ "$(cat "$C/harness.stamp" 2>/dev/null)" = "$KEY" ]; then
    CACHE=filled
else
    rm -rf "$C" ; mkdir -p "$C" ; printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$C/global.map" ; CACHE=empty
#!/bin/bash
# junit.sh <label> <dir-of-tests> <Name.test>... : the gather of climb batch N runs each .test through the
# harness in the main tree (fortress junit, the compiled test harness, as climb batch 6.5's gather ran its pair),
# in the order given, so that a link test runs before its XXX run test. Each named component's cache entries are
# removed before the list and after it. First line: the machine line (protocol.md, principle 2).
# ONE_JVM=1 (added 2026-09-29 for the repair on the merged tree, coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md, "A repair
# of tests and records only"): the whole list in one fortress junit run, one JVM, as the gate's track runs them
# together; Shell junit hands the list to FileTests.suiteFromListOfFiles (Shell.java:1086), which puts its
# compile and link tests before its run tests (FileTests.java:997-1004), so a link test still runs first.
# The environment is env.sh's, set here without sourcing it, since env.sh also removes parser directories in
# /tmp. The tree is the one this script is in. FORTRESS_THREADS=4 is the pin of build.xml's fastTrack macro,
# which runs the gate's compiled tracks. The JVMs keep their temporary files, parser directories among them,
# in the tree's tmp/.
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=4
mkdir -p "$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
FH=$FORTRESS_HOME; L=${1:?label}; D=$(cd "${2:?dir}" && pwd); shift 2
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress"
CP=$(../bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1)
echo "# junit.sh $L $(date -u +%FT%TZ); nproc $(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=$FORTRESS_THREADS; tree $(git -C $FH rev-parse --short HEAD)$(git -C $FH diff --quiet HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library || echo ' with the next rung applied, not yet committed'); tests from $D"
clean () { for t in "$@"; do n=$(sed -n 's/^tests=//p' "$D/$t" | head -1); [ -n "$n" ] && find ../default_repository/caches -name "*$n*" -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null; done; }
clean "$@"
if [ -n "${ONE_JVM:-}" ]; then
  files=(); for t in "$@"; do files+=("$D/$t"); done
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit, one JVM: $*"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "${files[@]}" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
